insight: Curaçao's performance in the 2026 World Cup has shown that hydration breaks can be a crucial factor in their gameplay, with the team gaining momentum in 4 out of 6 breaks, resulting in a slight increase in their overall performance. However, when Curaçao was pressing before a hydration break, they tended to lose momentum, with their performance declining by an average of 0.100 minutes, and they were only able to maintain their momentum once out of three times. In contrast, when they were not pressing before a break, they saw a significant improvement in their performance, with an average increase of 0.133 minutes, suggesting that the team is able to regroup and refocus during these breaks. This data suggests that Curaçao's strategy and performance can be heavily influenced by how they approach hydration breaks, and that they may benefit from adjusting their tactics
